kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth has an explicit depends_on on module.aws_eks, but that ordering is already implied transitively via its dependency on data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which depends on data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster and hence on module.aws_eks (and the cluster must exist and be reachable before the readiness probe succeeds).

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng has an explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.managed_ng, but the node_group_arn attribute already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng.arn, establishing the same dependency implicitly.

null_resource.update_trust_policy has an explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution, but the local-exec command already references ${aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id}, establishing the same dependency implicitly.

null_resource.update_trust_policy has an explicit depends_on on kubernetes_namespace.spark, but the local-exec command already references ${kubernetes_namespace.spark.id}, establishing the same dependency implicitly.

aws_eks_addon.vpc_cni has an explicit depends_on on module.irsa_addon, but service_account_role_arn already references module.irsa_addon.irsa_iam_role_arn, establishing the same dependency implicitly.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver has an explicit depends_on on module.irsa_addon, but service_account_role_arn already references module.irsa_addon.irsa_iam_role_arn, establishing the same dependency implicitly.

The aws-auth ConfigMap's mapRoles data aggregates role entries produced by module.aws_eks_teams (local.application_teams_config_map and local.platform_teams_config_map, which come from module.aws_eks_teams outputs). There is no attribute reference or depends_on connecting kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth to module.aws_eks_teams, so the ConfigMap can be applied before the platform/application team IAM roles exist, leaving those teams without cluster access until aws-auth is re-applied.
